notes.title: Status Update
notes.notes:
Hi everyone! We hope you’re all doing well. We’ve had some unexpected changes to our development schedule, but don’t worry, it’s nothing to be concerned about. As a result, we’ll be pausing our feature focuses for a while. You’ll likely see some updates similar to our monthly progress reports, but we can’t make any promises.

On a positive note, the progress on Rocket Engineer is going well. We’re fixing bugs and focusing heavily on improving the user experience. If you’d like to have an early access to the game and help us prepare it for a public release through testing, feel free to join the Discord server.

Thanks for following Rocket Engineer!

notes.title: March 2025 Progress Update
notes.notes:
[b]Was Rocket Engineer gone? Where were the developers? Where are we? Here we are!
[/b]

Yes, Rocket Engineer is back on track and more than alive! After a significant 9-month-long period without any progress updates, we are thrilled to announce that Rocket Engineer is back! In reality, Rocket Engineer had stopped development for only 5 months. Several factors could have easily killed the game, but thankfully, they didn’t.

In fact, since December, we have been working tirelessly to rework Rocket Engineer from the ground up. In just two months, we successfully reached feature parity (and even a bit more) with the previous code base that had 2 years of history.

Remaking Rocket Engineer has resulted in significantly more stable, scalable, and future-proof systems. It also allowed us to shift our focus from rocket design to colony and resource extraction. This shift has made the game more accessible and enjoyable, and we’re excited to continue pushing it further.

Over the next few weeks until April, we’ll be posting detailed updates on each new or reworked feature to give you more information and share more screenshots. One of the most important changes is the significant reduction in the size of Rocket Engineer’s solar system, which allows us to add much more detail to planets and moons.

We are incredibly proud to announce that Rocket Engineer is back on track and in its production phase. That means we’re focusing on polishing, fixing bugs, and ensuring that the game feels great to play. The game loop is already closed, but the first early access will only contain a sandbox mode where you have unlimited resources on Earth but will need to exploit resources everywhere else to expand your off-world colonies.

We will be very busy in the coming months. We don’t want to announce any release date yet, but we do have internal deadlines that we are confident about achieving.

Feel free to join our Discord if you want to stay updated on Rocket Engineer!
https://discord.gg/BkNjccBwDX

notes.title: July 2024 Progress Update
notes.notes:
Hi! We hope everyone is having a great summer. It’s time for a small update on how things are progressing for Rocket Engineer.

First things first, there were some changes of plans. Some feature that were planned to be added over the course of early access will be implemented at the early access release. It does result in a slightly longer delay than initially planned (see the previous development update) but is worth it. Over the next months you should see this change reflect on the Steam page.

During the month of June, we've implemented many quality of life improvements, small changes, and graphical enhancements. The most noticeable changes are the UI/UX rework on the main menu and the new atmosphere/planet shaders, and the camera controller has been updated to allow dragging to move the camera. 

The visual identity is currently being enforced as we implement new textures and update the UI to match it. A lot of the focus has shifted to improve the user experience and user interface.

This month saw the completion of the 0.1.x versions and the team has started working on the 0.2 which adds much more features.

Also, a new developer recently joined the team (rtificr), helping the development to go faster than before and making important changes.

Here's a small video featuring the atmospheres and their day/night cycle:
https://youtu.be/4ttQ5DMTxGg

notes.title: May 2024 Progress Update
notes.notes:
Hi everyone!
I hope you are all doing well, I have a few announcement to make. 

First things first, I had to take a hard decision but I believe I took the right choice. The game will [b]not release this summer[/b] and is therefore delayed. I currently have no date but I will give one as soon as I am able to provide it. The reason for this delay are not linked to technical issues but about [b]polishing. I want the user experience to be as good as possible[/b]. Due to this game complexity and its core gameplay it is making it hard, rocket science is rocket science. 

Also, another reason of the delay is that I and some testers are [b]working a lot on some of the most criticized aspects of the game[/b]. I currently cannot tell you what work was done this recent month about these things but it is looking really good.

To close on that subject, [b]progress updates will no longer be monthly[/b] and will only be published when there is interesting things to talk about.

As you might have predicted, [b]the public demo is also delayed to an unkown date[/b]. I still want to have something playable as soon as possible so I will try to give you something [b]this summer[/b].

This month was not the busiest one but you might have seen in a [b]video that was published this previous month [/b](which I will link below) that bugs have been significantly reduced and the experience significantly improved, to the point that it is playable. 

Finally, the [b]visual identity of Rocket Engineer has been reworked[/b]. There are still some things I need to convert to this new identity but I am very happy with the result.

Sneak Peak:
[previewyoutube=J5anaQ1-LTE;leftthumb][/previewyoutube]

notes.title: April 2024 Progress Update
notes.notes:
Hi!

Before we start talking about what progress has been made during the past month, I wanted to let you know that a public demo will be available in June! With that being said, let’s start!

Over the past month the game received its last major additions in term of physics model which is now stable and accurate. Also, a new version was published early in March. I received a lot of feedback which helped me to know what to prioritize. There is obviously still bugs and improvements to be made, but the list of game breaking bugs is definitely going down. 

Over the next month(s), the plan is to keep fixing the bugs and opening the test builds to more people. Furthermore, the goal is to also improve the UI, sounds and add a tutorial that explains enough so that the player is able to understand what he has to do. 

Thanks for reading! Seeing you soon!

notes.title: March 2024 Progress Update
notes.notes:
Hi everyone! I hope you’re all doing well as spring begins. Let’s dive right into what was done during February!

Early during the month I posted a first trailer for Rocket Engineer (see on the Steam page). The reception was truly incredible and I was not ready for such positive comments and definitely converted into more motivation to continue the development despite the various challenges encountered so far. Thanks a lot to all of view for watching it!

One feature that is very important, I’d even say crucial for Rocket Engineer realism and that any rocket or physics based game have are collisions that results sometimes into explosion. That is what was added and was very straight forward. In consequence, parachutes were added to allow a capsule to come back to Earth safely after a landing on the Moon. 

Also, a very important aspect is the map. Previously, the only things that were displayed were logos that showed the position of the planets, the rockets and rocket’s trajectories. However, this is not sufficient at all for even thinking about navigating to the Moon with an efficient rocket. Hence several functionalities were implemented:
[list]
[*] Rendering of the planet trajectory
[*] Rendering of the planet sphere of influence
[*] Detection of potential intercepts
[/list]
The last item, detection of potential intercepts, was especially hard since it had to iterate and be efficient but a very good solution was found which is both efficient and precise.

This intercept detection feature also resulted in fixes for the hyperbolic trajectories for on rail orbits which were not calculated as expected.

Another core feature to the physics system that was implemented is to let the player control a previously launched rocket/satellite and switch seamlessly between multiple sats/rockets. It took a lot of time to get right but works very well.

Finally, several minor things were done and lot of bug fixing, which definitely improve the user experience.

So, what’s next for March? I plan to continue on improving the user experience, finalize the rework of some systems, integrate a full tutorial and adding more sounds/musics. Hopefully, a version will be available for testers by mid-March. There might be a public demo around end of March or April but it still depends on a lot of things.

Thanks a lot for following the project, if you have any questions don’t hesitate!

notes.title: February 2024 Progress Update
notes.notes:
Hi!
During January a lot of progress was made. The game looks completely different from what it was previously. Here’s a small comparison: 

[b]Current[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44817196/e7dacecae12d83079ac3d98600c418742f1c6e80.png[/img]

[b]Previous[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44817196/9c768fa20fda74e30e4f7d613afc5a30c5a53ff6.png[/img]

So let’s start by what I started doing in January!

[b]Graphics[/b]

The idea behind choosing this art style was to contrast with the gameplay. A complex gameplay with a simplistic graphic style. This art style will also allow to focus much more on the code that makes Rocket Engineer alive while delivering a great variety of parts and features.

The hardest part of defining Rocket Engineer’s style was to find the right colour palette. Here’s a few early screenshots before the final colours were found:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44817196/a445bcb3264f6f9bfbf393de8de65ef66a1c996b.jpg[/img]
[i]The ground was obviously too green[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44817196/61d64ebacf7f7811218c64072e616d745a3a1d16.png[/img]
[i]Depth was missing and colours weren’t right, especially for the sky[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44817196/e2cee2cb8bad4129720d9fb962ffaa6d3f100a62.png[/img]
[i]The decal was just trying to mimic grass...[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44817196/c74b047fb9d49367ac0d62670ad93264c8c76370.png[/img]
[i]Pretty close, but the gradient wasn’t in the good order[/i]

Another difficult Rocket Engineer’s specific challenge is the fact that the parts doesn’t always have fixed sizes. A good example are rocket’s fuel tank which width and height are determined by the player. That meant that I had to implement a script that would automatically scale and position the shadow accordingly. It is still in progress but gave good results so far. Another thing that has to be done due to this scalability of tanks is that I have to sometime hide the rounded corners of the tank if another tank is on top of it so that the visuals are consistent.

[b]UI[/b]

Following this iteration through the design of the visuals, I decided to work on the UI. UI for this type of game have to be intuitive and really good. My goal is to have as little tutorial as possible by having a very good UI design. I have still not yet reached that goal but I am getting closer. The main challenge is to give as much information as possible when the player needs it in a good way. 

Such example is the fuel tank UI which is in the world space:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44817196/c51e8937d13887fcafed85c7485f0d4fa7621268.png[/img]
The reason for making it world space is that the player actively need to look at it while filling the rocket and sometime several of them are acting at the same time. The gauge helps to quickly see if the maximum volume have been reached. 

Speaking of gauges, you might have seen that they were not present for the fuel tanks connected to the rocket. That decision was made because the UI is not world space and has much more little space to work with. However, as feedback will come in, that might still change.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44817196/e7dacecae12d83079ac3d98600c418742f1c6e80.png[/img]
[i]At the right of the screen you can see the rocket UI with its stages[/i]

Once the UI reached a good quality I started working on the animations. Honestly, it did a massive difference and I even ended up pressing a button multiple times just to see the animation going on. Adding animations added a lot of depth.

[b]Particle Effects[/b]
Particle effects are super important for Rocket Engineer. They allow to visually communicate the state of objects and provide a direct feedback to the player. A good example is the venting on the fuel tanks (as seen in previous screenshots). This communicates that the current state is either gaseous or really cold (LOX). Moreover, I wanted the venting to persist on the ground as we can see for different rockets launch so I tweaked it a bit to really get this effect. In the end it also adds a dramatic effect to your launch and makes the rocket look more alive.

Of course, another important particle effect is the engine’s plume. It is still work in progress but definitely makes the game look more alive. In the future, when more propellant combinations will be in game, the colour will varies depending on these. Here’s a look at the engine in action:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44817196/ed5442f5c6c98fb0f4b82f0ef2c11e4c7b3bd697.png[/img]

Finally another effect that was added were explosion, but it really is still in progress.

I’ll link a video at the end if you’re interested in seeing more.

[b]Other Small Artistic Progess[/b]
Some other small things that are still in progress is that I started adding sounds which adds even more depth and button clicking addiction than animations and makes static fires sounds nice. For engines, I activated the spatialization of audio, meaning that the static fires will be heard more or less depending on how far you are from it, which I think sounds very nice.

[b]Progress on the coding side[/b]
Prediction and timewarp are now much more reliable than before. Drag was added back and improve the experience significantly. The transfer from a celestial body to another caused significant bugs and is now working reliably. The fuel system was fully reworked to be more stable and static fires, which were full of bugs, are now much more stable.

[b]Testing[/b]
A first version with these visuals improvements was sent to the testers and the feedback really helped to determine the priorities and know what was right... or wrong. Thanks a lot to them!

[b]So... what’s next?[/b] 
Currently, I am focusing on improving the audio experience and adding more variety to the engines parts to have a trailer ready. Around end of February or March I plan to publish a first public demo. Lot of work is still required but at the pace at which I’m progressing it is still very possible. That will allow to have the first “large-scale” feedback and first impressions.

Thanks for reading! If you haven’t done yet, wishlist Rocket Engineer, it really helps. If you want to follow the development more closely, join the discord server: https://discord.gg/4khHZyPaKp

Here’s a small gameplay video that was sent to the testers which might interest you. Note that it was a while ago and the bugs seen were fixed, it really is just there if you want to see more:
[url=https://youtu.be/cHVdcqftuGQ]click here to see the video![/url]
